$comment: GENERATED companion to docs/radio-addressing.md. That document is normative; this file is the machine-readable contract other repos assert against. Do not hand-edit.

algorithm.decode: n = 0; for p in 0..4: n = n*5 + index_in_alphabet(name[p])
algorithm.normalize: trim ASCII whitespace; map A-Z to a-z
algorithm.encode: n -> name, the inverse of decode: for p = 4 down to 0: name[p] = alphabet(p)[n % 5]; n = n / 5
algorithm.endianness: name[0] is the MOST significant base-5 digit and name[4] the LEAST. Base-5 conversion naturally emits least-significant first, so a naive encoder produces reversed names: n=1 is 'zuzuv', not 'vuzuz'. The error is diagnostic-free -- 3125 well-formed, regex-passing, distinct names in the wrong order.

channel.note: 25 is a VALID channel and zeguz occupies it

why.10: microbit-radio-relay's !C button space forces group 10 across channels 0-35

properties.full_space_canonical_form: for n = 0..3124 in order, one line '<name>,<channel>,<group>\n', UTF-8, sha256 of the concatenation

endianness_probe.why: Digit-palindrome names are IDENTICAL under both orderings and cannot detect a reversed encoder. zuzuz, tatat, zotoz and pipip are all palindromes -- including both extremes, which is what an implementer reaches for first. zotuz (n=225) reverses to zutoz and is the published vector that catches it.
endianness_probe.reversed_encoder_digest_note: If your digest equals THIS value, your encoder is little-endian; reverse the digit order.

vectors.name: zuzuv
vectors.note: n=1, the simplest ASYMMETRIC vector: reverses to vuzuz, so it fails loudly against a little-endian encoder where zuzuz and tatat both pass

vectors.note: group-skip boundary; would have been group 10
